name: imgproc
algorithm: Run the imgproc dogfood's bench pipeline (blur, sharpen, equalize, sobel, resize, gamma, a channel swap, posterize, gray, dilate and threshold) over its in-memory colour test pattern at a larger size, then print the result's statistics (README.md).
notes: Tier A (M9 item 11.32): an Mk-only row, the imgproc dogfood unchanged, compared across mk binaries; no twin, no peer, no defect line (README.md).

Labelled: imgproc writes its own vector code (std.simd's Vec) and chooses its kernel path at run time (--path auto, its Cpu() dispatch in its unsafe module src/dispatch), which keeps it out of a twinned row unchanged (D-781). So the path it times is the machine's widest, and a comparison is between two mk binaries on one machine only.

The quick arguments are the dogfood's own bench case (Dogfoods/imgproc/cases/bench.args); the publish arguments make the pattern 4096x4096 and resize it to 2048 wide. imgproc refuses a pattern of more than 67,108,864 samples (its pnm.MaxSamples, three per pixel), so 6144x4608 is refused, with a message that names only the 16,384 side limit (seen at 6144x4096 and 6144x4608; the dogfood is used unchanged).
The size is provisional; tools/bench verify -publish-size fixes it in the quiet window, and the checksum changes with it.
